name: cpu_robot_control
title: Real time robot control
short_description: Fixed rate control loop with robot dynamics and model predictive control.

structured_text.description: Runs the control loop of a bundled robot arm model at a fixed rate on one core: rigid body dynamics with Pinocchio and a model predictive controller solved with OSQP in every cycle. Instead of throughput the test records how long each cycle takes, because a controller that misses its deadline makes the robot stutter or fault.
structured_text.metric_explanation: The score is the 99.9th percentile of the control cycle time, in nanoseconds.
structured_text.value_interpretation: Lower is better. Shorter and steadier cycle times allow higher control rates and more headroom before a deadline is missed.
structured_text.reasoning: Real time control depends on single core speed, cache behaviour and how steady the system responds, not on peak throughput. A tail latency score captures the stutter that average speed hides.
